title: "Convolve RMS energy with an SPMG1 HRF"

sidebar: cookbook

## Use when

You have a continuous acoustic feature such as RMS energy and want a
hemodynamic regressor on the scan TR grid. Extraction stays in
`natural_features`. Convolution belongs in [fmrimod](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod).

This page uses TR = 2 s, stimulus onset at scan t = 0.67 s, and fmrimod's
`spmg1` canonical HRF. The executed cells use a short synthetic WAV so the
docs site can render without a large local recording.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "figure.facecolor": "#111827",
        "axes.facecolor": "#111827",
        "axes.edgecolor": "#9ca3af",
        "axes.labelcolor": "#e5e7eb",
        "axes.titlecolor": "#f9fafb",
        "xtick.color": "#d1d5db",
        "ytick.color": "#d1d5db",
        "grid.color": "#374151",
        "text.color": "#f9fafb",
        "legend.facecolor": "#111827",
        "legend.edgecolor": "#4b5563",
    }
)
```

```{python}
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from natural_features import (
    ClockMap,
    TemporalContext,
    extract_features,
    temporal_object_in_clock,
)
from natural_features.fmri.compat import has_fmrimod, hrf_regressor

tr_s = 2.0
stim_onset_s = 0.67
sr_hz = 8000
duration_s = 16.0

t = np.arange(int(duration_s * sr_hz), dtype=np.float32) / sr_hz
envelope = np.full(t.shape, 0.03, dtype=np.float32)
envelope[(t >= 4.0) & (t < 10.0)] = 0.35
samples = envelope * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 220.0 * t)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    wav_path = Path(tmp) / "soundtrack.wav"
    pcm = np.asarray(np.clip(samples, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0, dtype="<i2")
    with wave.open(str(wav_path), "wb") as wav:
        wav.setnchannels(1)
        wav.setsampwidth(2)
        wav.setframerate(sr_hz)
        wav.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
    result = extract_features(wav_path, features=["audio.rms"])

rms = result.features["audio.rms"]
n_trs = int(np.ceil((stim_onset_s + duration_s) / tr_s))
rms_scan = temporal_object_in_clock(
    rms,
    "scan:run-01",
    context=TemporalContext(
        (ClockMap("stimulus", "scan:run-01", offset_s=stim_onset_s),)
    ),
)
```

## Original feature, then SPMG1

Native RMS remains one row every 10 ms. `hrf_regressor()`
passes those samples to `fmrimod.regressor(..., hrf="spmg1")` as weighted
impulses of mass `rms * hop_s`, then evaluates the convolution on the scan
grid.

```{python}
if has_fmrimod():
    bold = hrf_regressor(
        rms_scan,
        tr_s=tr_s,
        n_scans=n_trs,
        hrf="spmg1",
        start_time=0.0,
    )
    summary = {
        "native_rows": int(rms.values.shape[0]),
        "native_hop_s": rms.timebase.hop_s,
        "n_trs": int(bold.values.shape[0]),
        "tr_times_s": bold.times_s.tolist(),
        "spmg1_peak_s": float(bold.times_s[int(np.argmax(bold.values[:, 0]))]),
    }
else:
    bold = None
    summary = {
        "native_rows": int(rms.values.shape[0]),
        "native_hop_s": rms.timebase.hop_s,
        "fmrimod": "not installed; convolution skipped",
    }
summary
```

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.2, 5.2), sharex=True)
axes[0].plot(rms_scan.times_s, rms.values[:, 0], color="#93c5fd", lw=1.0, label="native RMS")
axes[0].axvline(stim_onset_s, color="#f9a8d4", ls="--", lw=1.0, label="audio t=0")
axes[0].set_ylabel("RMS")
axes[0].set_title("Original feature time series")
axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.35)
axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)

if bold is not None:
    axes[1].plot(
        bold.times_s,
        bold.values[:, 0],
        color="#34d399",
        marker="o",
        lw=1.6,
        label="SPMG1 regressor",
    )
    axes[1].set_title("fmrimod SPMG1-convolved regressor")
else:
    axes[1].text(
        0.5,
        0.5,
        "Install fmrimod to compute the SPMG1 regressor",
        ha="center",
        va="center",
        transform=axes[1].transAxes,
    )
    axes[1].set_title("SPMG1-convolved regressor")
axes[1].axvline(stim_onset_s, color="#f9a8d4", ls="--", lw=1.0)
axes[1].set_xlabel("scan time (s)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("predicted BOLD")
axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.35)
if bold is not None:
    axes[1].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig
```

The lower trace is delayed and smoothed relative to RMS. That lag is the
canonical SPM hemodynamic response, not a shift applied to the feature
times. Loud RMS occupies audio 4–10 s (scan 4.67–10.67 s); the SPMG1 peak
falls several seconds later.

Install fmrimod from source when it is not already on `PYTHONPATH`:

```bash
python -m pip install "fmrimod @ git+https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod.git"
```

A command-line wrapper for a local soundtrack is
`examples/rms_spmg1_hrf.py`.
